meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 13: Extensions (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about extension negotiation are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: An empty settings object means supported with no additional settings
A breaking change to an extension reuses its identifier with a new version field
Extensions are enabled by default once both SDKs support them
Servers advertise them in the capabilities returned by server/discover
Clients advertise extensions in clientCapabilities.extensions on each request

questions.explanation: A, B and C are the mechanics. Extensions are always disabled by default and require explicit opt-in, and an unavoidable breaking change takes a new identifier, such as one suffixed -v2.

questions.question: Which statements correctly separate core MRTR from the Tasks extension? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: MRTR is core and must be implemented; Tasks is opt-in on both sides
MRTR continues by retrying the original request; Tasks continues with tasks/update
Both signal with resultType "input_required" on the original response
MRTR needs no server-side state; a task is durably created before its result is sent
Both require the client to poll repeatedly for the final result

questions.explanation: Tasks signal with resultType "task" (a CreateTaskResult) and only then report input_required inside tasks/get, so D is wrong. Only Tasks involves polling; MRTR's answer arrives as the retry's response.
